investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's official 'À l'affiche' listing page, then against one show's own detail page (still Level 1 — a second plain page fetch, not an escalation) to confirm what time-of-day/price data this source's own two-page structure exposes.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.ledomedeparis.com/fr/spectacles/a-laffiche immediately exposed 26 real, current, repeated static-HTML event cards, each with a title, a self-stated category (Concert/Comédie musicale/One man show/Spectacle), a French date text, and a stable numeric-id permalink. A second plain GET of one card's own detail page (/fr/spectacle/337/cheb-mami) confirmed this source's own two-page structure: the listing page carries title/date/category/url, and each event's own detail page separately carries time-of-day and a full price breakdown. No JS execution or further escalation was needed at any point.

venue_reference: Le Dôme de Paris (Palais des Sports), 34 Boulevard Victor, 75015 Paris

identity.notes: The retained listing page's own <title> reads 'Tous les spectacles à l'affiche - Dôme de Paris' at the venue's own domain ledomedeparis.com. The same page embeds a real, rendered (not commented-out) Google Maps iframe whose own query string directly names the pinned place 'Le+Dome+de+Paris' at coordinates matching the assigned venue reference's known 15th-arrondissement (Porte de Versailles) location. A separate address text ('34 Boulevard Victor - 75015 Paris') is also present in the retained HTML but inside an HTML comment (a currently-disabled footer block) — noted honestly as present-but-not-rendered, not relied on alone for identity.

site_classification.platform: Custom/bespoke CMS (no WordPress/wp-content/wp-json signal detected). The listing page repeats one real static HTML card per show; each card links to its own first-party detail page (also static HTML) carrying time-of-day and price. Ticket sales are routed to Ticketmaster (an external platform, linked per-detail-page) — the FACTS this source exposes (title/date/category/time/price) are this venue's own first-party markup across its two own pages, not scraped from Ticketmaster.

title.notes: Each listing card's own `<h4>` link text, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Single-day cards state the full date directly in one field (e.g. 'CHEB MAMI': '05 septembre 2026' — DIRECT_SOURCE, no derivation needed). Multi-day cards (e.g. 'LE ROI SOLEIL': 'Du 12 septembre au 18 octobre 2026') state the row's own year exactly once, trailing the second date, which governs the leading (start) date's own omitted month/year within the SAME retained row — verified mechanically reproducible across every one of the 26 real retained cards, including day-only leading fragments (e.g. 'Du 06 au 07 novembre 2026') (tests/dome-de-paris.test.mjs). This DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT case is used as this field's representative value since it is the stricter policy-relevant case; the simpler DIRECT_SOURCE single-day case is also fully proven in the same test file.

derivation.rule: within one 'Du D1 [Month1] au D2 Month2 YYYY' listing-card row, the single trailing 'Month2 YYYY' fragment governs any month/year the leading D1 fragment itself omits (day-only, or day+month with no year stated) — applied only to this exact 'Du ... au ...' row shape, never across different rows.
inputs: leading date fragment (this row's own start): '12 septembre' — day+month, no year stated
trailing date fragment (this row's own end): '18 octobre 2026' — day+month+year, supplying the governing year

time.value: 20:00 (Europe/Paris, floating local — no explicit UTC offset anywhere in this field)
time.notes: Not present on the listing page at all — stated directly on the event's own detail page instead, in a 'Horaires et dates des représentations' block ('Samedi 5 septembre 2026 - 20:00'). A doors-opening time ('Ouverture des portes à 19:00') is also directly present and distinct from the performance start time. This is a genuinely two-page source: a collector needs the per-event detail page for time (and price, below), not just the listing page.

end.notes: For a multi-day run, the listing card's own trailing date fragment directly states a distinct end date (e.g. 'LE ROI SOLEIL' -> end 2026-10-18, DIRECT_SOURCE, no derivation needed for the end value itself — only the START's missing month/year required the DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT combination described above). The majority of cards (single-day shows) state no distinct end date/time at all. Because presence is genuinely conditional on the card's own shape, this is honestly recorded PARTIAL rather than claiming one universal value.

venue_location.notes: Not stated per-card/per-detail-page as a discrete field beyond generic site branding. This source represents exactly one physical venue (Le Dôme de Paris, 34 Boulevard Victor) — consistent with the badehaus-berlin-01/zenner-berlin-01 precedent, venue identity is intended to resolve via source_id at activation time.

source_record_id.notes: This source's own permalink scheme, `/fr/spectacle/{numeric_id}/{slug}`, is this venue's own canonical, self-consistent path for every listed show — the same documented judgement already established for badehaus-berlin-01/le-grand-rex-paris-01 (a source's own permalink identity is a proven stable identifier).

event_url.notes: Each card's own permalink href, stated directly — this venue's own first-party show page (ticket purchase itself then routes onward to Ticketmaster from that page, but the event_url recorded here is this source's own page).

price.value: Prestige : 95€; Carré Or : 79€; Catégorie 1 : 69€; Catégorie 2 : 59€; Catégorie 3 : 49€; PMR : gratuit
price.notes: Not present on the listing page — stated directly on the event's own detail page instead, in a 'Prix des places' block. Same two-page caveat as `time` above.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, and a real rendered Google Maps embed directly naming this exact venue at its known location).
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML, a resolved supported class, reached at Level 1 with no escalation needed.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained for both the listing page (26 real, current cards) and one representative detail page.

title PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE; start_date PROVEN with basis DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT for the stricter multi-day case (a documented, reproducible, single mechanical combination rule, offline-proven across all 26 real retained cards) and DIRECT_SOURCE for the simpler single-day case.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own numeric permalink.

This venue's own card carries a real, self-stated 'Concert' category distinguishing it from its own 'Comédie musicale'/'One man show'/'Spectacle' categories — isConcertCard() in ingestion/dome-de-paris/observation-adapter.mjs implements this as an explicit, never-silent filter using the source's own classification.

PARIS_BESPOKE: no existing collector family in this project matches this exact two-page (listing + per-event detail) static HTML shape; a new, small, bespoke module was written (ingestion/dome-de-paris/observation-adapter.mjs).

DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence retained (tests/dome-de-paris.test.mjs, 9 passing assertions re-parsing both retained fixtures deterministically, including every one of the 26 real listing dates and the detail-page time/price extraction).
